cards.rationale: Exact preimage and candidate hashes verified. Res Gestae 21 says Augustus built the Forum of Augustus and temple of Mars Ultor on his own land from war spoils; the answer and explanation are accurate. Each option is a Roman public place, and notes are individually factual. This is distinct from 078’s Athenian boundary stone and 080/081’s institutions.

Exact hashes verified. Tacitus Annals 1.8 says the first Senate meeting after Augustus’s death discussed only his funeral; proposals included the triumphal arch and list of conquests, matching prompt and explanation. The four options are Roman political bodies. Easy fits the clear primary passage and alternatives.

Exact hashes verified. Aristotle, Constitution 43, says the sovereign Assembly in each prytany considered magistrates’ performance, grain supply, and defense of the country. The question identifies the specific body and agenda; the explanation adds the vote on officials. It is distinct from 019’s paid attendance as evidence for democracy and from 078’s Agora boundary stone: neither gives this agenda/body relation. The institutional distractors and their notes are specific and plausible.

Exact hashes verified. The Met catalogue identifies the object as a Rhodian terracotta amphora fragment; the handle has the rose stamp, Xenophantos and month Sminthios, plus the side beta stamp. Candidate key and explanation match. The three vessel distractors and notes are separate objects/functions; easy is reasonable from the exact catalogue clues.

Exact hashes verified. The London Museum record calls it a ceramic factory lamp and describes its elongated nozzle, shoulder lugs and FORTIS stamp on the base. Prompt and answer are supported. The other options are vessels or writing objects, each with a distinct checked note; easy suits identification from the wick nozzle and stamp.

Exact hashes verified. The Met describes this Roman gold crossbow fibula as a cloak fastener; the inscription reads “HERCVLI AVGVSTE SEMPER VINCAS” and the titles probably refer to Maximian. Candidate wording and explanation correctly preserve the museum’s uncertainty. Jewelry options are comparable and separately supported; medium is apt for the specific artifact/type.

Exact hashes verified. The Odyssey passage has Penelope set up a loom to weave Laertes’s shroud by day and unravel it by night. The supplied Theoi page returned 403 in the review tool; an academic Perseus copy of Odyssey 2.94–105 independently confirms the same passage and key. The mechanism and other options are distinct; the easy level is supported by the recognizable narrative clue.

Exact hashes verified. The official Ostia Antica Caseggiato degli Aurighi page states that apartments for rent and service rooms occupied several floors facing a large central courtyard; it also records preserved painted decoration. The exact official page timed out on direct open, but its indexed content returned the full description, and the official English district page independently places the Aurighi building among large multi-storey residential complexes. Insula is a defensible general category; distinct from 069 basilica and 070 thermae, which identify different sites/building types.

Exact hashes verified. The Vatican Museums page identifies the Canopus/Serapeum as part of Hadrian’s Villa at Tivoli, and notes that the Serapeum interpretation has been questioned in recent years; the candidate carefully says the structure is “commonly called” the Serapeum and does not present the disputed interpretation as certain. This is a villa, distinct from the specific basilica/thermae questions 069–070 and the residential insula 086. Medium fits a site-specific classification.

Exact hashes verified. Livius reproduces Behistun §45: Darius calls Vivana his satrap of Arachosia; the key satrapy is sound. The prompt asks for the administrative unit without naming “satrapy”; it is a specific Behistun example, distinct from 089–091’s Roman province, Egyptian nome, and independent polis examples. However answer option 2’s current note attributes “priests from temples of Egyptian nomes gathered at Canopus” to the Canopus Decree, whose exact translation names sanctuaries of Upper and Lower Egypt at Peguat but does not mention nomes. Direct one-field FIX to replace only this note with the generic, independently supported UCL Digital Egypt definition. Other answer notes and item content remain unchanged.
cards.directedFix: Один directed cycle только для answers[2].note: заменить «Канопский декрет упоминает жрецов из храмов египетских номов, собравшихся в Канопе.» на «Номом в египтологии называют провинцию Древнего Египта.» Опора: University College London, Digital Egypt, “Provinces of Egypt” (https://www.ucl.ac.uk/museums-static/digitalegypt/geo/index.html), который определяет nome как египетскую провинцию. Не менять остальные поля, difficulty, correctIndex или источник карточки для основного вопроса.
